parsed.basis: Lesotho does not criminalise consensual same-sex conduct, and no trans-specific criminal offence is documented, but there is no general anti-discrimination protection beyond employment, no way to change a legal gender marker, and a transgender visitor travelling on a passport mismatched to presentation could face questioning or charges. Discrimination, rape and assaults are documented, with stigma and under-reporting, alongside a registered LGBTI organisation active nationally and at times supportive police engagement concentrated around Maseru. Butha-Buthe is a rural northern district with strong traditional and church influence, small-community visibility, limited anonymity, and limited local legal, health and support services at distance from the capital, so discovery is more likely to become community-facing and recourse slower, with no district-specific protective exception known.
